summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of coronary artery disease presented with acute chest pain that occurred during dialysis and recurred at rest, relieved by sublingual nitroglycerin. The pain was consistent with angina, though serial troponins were negative and EKG showed no acute changes. He also reported a five-day history of non-bloody, non-febrile diarrhea, which resolved during the admission. He remained stable without further episodes of chest pain, was started on isosorbide mononitrate (Imdur) for angina prophylaxis, and continued all baseline medications. He was discharged home with instructions to follow up in cardiology and resume regular dialysis, with no complications during the hospital stay.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
